segments.text: In Medicare Advantage alone, health plans made fifty-three million prior-authorization decisions in 2024. Only eleven and a half percent of denials were appealed. Eighty-one percent of those appeals won. Millions of winnable denials are never contested, because appealing is paperwork.

This is Maya. Her plan denied her knee MRI: conservative therapy not documented, after eight weeks of physical therapy. Here is a browser-automation agent, with no WebMCP, trying to appeal on today's portal. It finds the denial. It opens the letter: two pages of prose to read and guess from. It finds the form: six pages, blue or black ink. Then it reaches the instructions: mail it, or fax it. No agent can fax. Every automated run stops here, exactly where people do.

Since January 2026, federal rule CMS-0057-F requires plans to decide prior authorizations within seven days, and by 2027 to expose them through a structured API. The plan side is being made machine-readable by law. Nobody is building the member's side.

Same portal, same account, now with WebMCP site tools. The agent reads the structured denial and the plan's own five criteria, and sees which of Maya's records support each one. It opens the appeal and drafts one argument per criterion, citing her records by name. The draft lands on the page, labelled drafted by your agent, every sentence editable. Completeness: zero of five, because attaching a record is Maya's job. She attaches her therapy notes, the orthopedic note and her medication history, and rewrites one argument in her own words. The agent notices, re-checks, five of five, and proposes expedited review. Her call. Then it asks to submit. It cannot submit. It can only ask. Maya signs. Case number, seventy-two-hour clock, and the tool surface changes: drafting tools out, status tools in. Every action is on the page.

The impact. For members: three point six million winnable denials a year that nobody files today, each now a single sitting. For health plans: the 2027 mandate arrives regardless; an agent-native portal turns compliance into a product. And the pattern repeats. Every claim-shaped dispute, from benefits to billing to property and auto, has the same shape: structured reads, drafted proposals, one human signature.
Overturn. Your agent does the paperwork on the plan's own portal. You make the decisions that are yours. Built for the WebMCP Challenge by Prathap, Rajani and Chitral. Open source, MIT.
